title: Update on Investigations into Alleged Mistreatment of Children at Centres of Preschool Chain
what_it_is: Update on Investigations into Alleged Mistreatment of Children at Centres of Preschool Chain

sections.label: Childcare mistreatment investigations update
sections.summary: Asks for updates on investigations into alleged childcare mistreatment, how ECEA will improve teacher standards and child safety, and whistle-blower protection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) whether an update can be provided on the findings from investigations carried out into the alleged mistreatment of children at childcare centres run by a local preschool provider reported in August 2023; (b) how will the Early Childhood Education Agency improve the standards of childcare teachers and the overall safety for children attending childcare centres; and (c) how will whistle-blowers reporting alleged mistreatment of children at childcare centres be protected.

sections.label: Preschool teacher arrests measures
sections.summary: Asks what measures address the arrests of two preschool teachers, the Ministry's strategy for secure early childhood environments, and efforts to educate on reporting abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development in view of the arrests of two preschool teachers for their suspected involvement in the ill-treatment of young children (a) what are the measures taken to address the situation promptly and thoroughly; (b) what is the Ministry’s broader strategy to cultivate a secure and nurturing environment in early childhood education institutions; and (c) what are the ongoing efforts to educate teachers, parents and students to recognise and report potential instances of abuse.

sections.label: Penalties for negligent preschool operators
sections.summary: Asks whether $5,000 penalties and reduced licence tenure are sufficient to discipline negligent preschool operators and whether penalties need further enhancement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) whether the penalties of $5,000 and reduced licence tenure are sufficient to discipline negligent preschool operators; and (b) whether there is a need to further enhance penalties under the relevant legislation and regulations.

sections.label: Reported childcare abuse case numbers
sections.summary: Asks how many rough handling or abuse cases at childcare centres were reported to ECDA in the past three years and how many led to dismissal or conviction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) in each of the past three years, how many cases of rough handling or abuse at childcare centres were reported to ECDA for investigations; and (b) what proportion of such investigations eventually led to a dismissal or criminal conviction.

sections.label: ECDA prevention and supervision questions
sections.summary: Asks how ECDA will prevent future abuse, balance stakeholder interests, tighten supervision and audit checks, and whether accused teachers face immediate suspension.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development in light of the recent incidents of alleged abuses in two preschools (a) how does ECDA intend to prevent similar incidents from happening in future; and (b) how does ECDA rationalise the actions it is taking while balancing the interests of all stakeholders in the preschools including parents, children, teachers, staff and preschool operators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development whether there is a need to tighten ECDA’s supervisory regime and increase the frequency of its unannounced audit checks on childcare centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) whether ECDA's current standard operating procedure requires the immediate suspension of a teacher accused of abusing a preschooler to prevent the teacher from being transferred to another childcare centre or working for a different operator while under investigation; and (b) if not, whether ECDA will consider doing so.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: If their questions have been addressed, it may not be necessary for them to proceed with these questions for future Sittings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: This incident and the others at the Kinderland centres should not have happened.

sections.label: ECDA multi-layered safeguards with sector
sections.summary: States ECDA will work closely with the preschool sector to strengthen the multi-layered safeguards system built over the years to prevent such incidents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: To prevent such incidents from happening, the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) will work closely with the preschool sector to strengthen our system of multi-layered safeguards which has been built up over the years.

sections.label: ECDA action against breaches
sections.summary: ECDA will act against operators and educators who breach requirements in the Act, Regulations or Code of Practice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: ECDA will take action against operators and educators found to have breached any of these requirements, whether in the Act, Regulations or Code of Practice.

sections.label: Strengthening educator training programmes
sections.summary: ECDA will work with NIEC and other training providers to strengthen programmes so educators know their child safety duties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Moving forward, ECDA will work with the National Institute of Early Childhood Development (NIEC) and other training providers to strengthen training programmes so that all educators are clear of their duty and obligations to ensure child safety.

sections.label: Unannounced preschool visits frequency
sections.summary: Unannounced visits to preschools are conducted on average once a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Unannounced visits to preschools are conducted on average once a year.

sections.label: Operator incident notification requirement
sections.summary: Operators must notify ECDA within 24 hours of incidents affecting children's health and safety or alleged staff child mismanagement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: When an incident affecting the health and safety of children or involving alleged child mismanagement by any staff occurs, the operator must notify ECDA within 24 hours.

sections.label: Mandatory preschool CCTV cameras
sections.summary: ECDA announced CCTV camera installation will be mandatory in all preschools from 1 July 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: ECDA has announced that the installation of CCTV cameras will be made mandatory in all preschools from 1 July 2024.

sections.label: Substantiated child mismanagement case rates
sections.summary: There are about 10 substantiated child mismanagement cases per 100,000 enrolled children yearly, a figure low and stable recently.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Ms Mariam Jaafar and Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim asked about the frequency of child mismanagement incidents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: There are about 10 substantiated cases per 100,000 enrolled children each year and this figure has remained low and stable over recent years.

sections.label: Kinderland fine and licence
sections.summary: Kinderland @ Woodlands Mart was fined $5,000, had its licence tenure cut to six months and its SPARK certification withdrawn, and ECDA intends to review penalty provisions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: For Kinderland @ Woodlands Mart, the operator was fined $5,000 and this is the maximum permitted under current laws.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: It also had its licence tenure reduced to six months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: ECDA has also withdrawn the centre’s Singapore Preschool Accreditation Framework (SPARK) certification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: With the experience gained in operationalising this regulatory framework, ECDA intends to strengthen the framework and review the provisions to see if penalties imposed on operators for child mismanagement should be enhanced, including whether financial penalties should be raised.

sections.label: Good Practices Guide launch
sections.summary: ECDA launched a Good Practices Guide to help operators implement workplace and human resources practices supporting staff well-being.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: To help operators support their employees, ECDA has launched a Good Practices Guide to guide them in implementing best workplace and human resources practices to foster a supportive work environment and support the well-being of their staff.

sections.label: ECDA three measures
sections.summary: ECDA will strengthen its investigation protocol, enhance its regulatory framework including penalty provisions, and work with NIEC and training providers on educator training.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: First, ECDA will strengthen its investigation protocol to ensure better oversight of cases under investigation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Second, we will enhance our regulatory framework, which includes a review of the penalty provisions for errant operators.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Third, we will work with NIEC and training providers to strengthen educator training in both prohibited and positive child management strategies so that educators are better equipped to ensure child safety.

sections.label: CCTV mandate timing question
sections.summary: The passage asks when exactly ECDA decided to mandate the installation of CCTVs in preschools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The first is: when exactly did ECDA decide to mandate the installation of CCTVs in preschools?

sections.label: CCTV plan and installation
sections.summary: The passage states the CCTV plan was made since last year and that ECDA's release said more than 60% of preschools already have them installed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, in the 31 August 2023 ECDA response and as shared by the Minister of State, this is something which was planned since last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, in ECDA's release, it was also said that more than 60% of preschools already have them installed.

sections.label: CCTV tracking and compliance
sections.summary: The passage states ECDA did not track installation pace or which preschools installed CCTVs before, and will work with operators after the deadline to ensure compliance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Then the follow-up question from that would seem to be, "If you have not installed, then does it mean that it is a bad thing?" So, we do not track and monitor the pace as well as which preschools have installed because this was not a mandated policy before.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: But now that we have announced that it will be mandatory, we will be working with the operators moving forward, after the installation deadline, to ensure that they comply.

sections.label: CCTV coverage in preschools
sections.summary: 60% of preschool operators have CCTVs, and it is almost 100% for EI centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Currently, already 60% of preschool operators have CCTVs and it is almost 100% for EI centres.

sections.label: Kinderland licence tenure reduction
sections.summary: ECDA reduced Kinderland's licence tenure by up to six months and may not renew it without significant improvements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The first pertains to ECDA's reduction of Kinderland's licence tenure of up to six months and I understand that ECDA will not hesitate to not renew the licence if the centre fails to demonstrate significant improvements.

sections.label: Tampering with CCTV footage
sections.summary: It will be an offence to tamper with CCTV footage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: On the second point, it will be an offence to tamper with CCTV footage.

sections.label: Staff training and development
sections.summary: Operators must conduct ongoing training and development for staff on child-safe policies and standards of care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Operators are also required to conduct ongoing training and provide development opportunities for staff to maintain their knowledge of child-safe policies and also their expected standards of care and appropriate behaviours in relation to children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I had mentioned in my main response that as part of our regular review and the lessons that we will learn from these unfortunate incidents, that ECDA will be working closely with NIEC and other training providers to strengthen training for our educators, whether or not these are new joiners, recent graduates or these are staff who have converted, moved from another industry into the preschool sector.

sections.label: Penalties on the operator
sections.summary: The operator received a $5,000 maximum financial penalty and its Centre's licence was reduced to six months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: As I have mentioned in my main reply, the penalties that have been imposed on the operator include a financial penalty of $5,000 and this is the maximum allowed under the current framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I have also shared that ECDA, arising from this case, will be reviewing the framework to see whether the financial penalty is sufficient and if need be, we will be looking to raise this financial penalty.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: This operator has also had its Centre's licence reduced to six months.

sections.label: Educator barred from childcare sector
sections.summary: ECDA has barred one of the educators from ever working in the childcare sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: ECDA has barred one of the educators from ever working in the childcare sector.

sections.label: ECDA workplace practices and well-being
sections.summary: ECDA launched a good practices guide for operators and is working with HPB and the Workplace Safety and Health Council on well-being programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: ECDA has launched a good practices guide to guide our operators in implementing best workplace and human resources practices to foster a supportive work environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: And ECDA is also working with HPB and the Workplace Safety and Health Council to offer programmes to operators and educators to support their overall well-being.

sections.label: Mandated CCTV for child safety
sections.summary: CCTV installation is mandated so feedback and incidents in childcare centres can be supported by evidence for investigations and parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: On the Member's question as to how we can ensure that not only our children's safety is being taken care of but also that we have policies in place for our educators, that is precisely why we have mandated CCTV installation so that when there is feedback, that there are unfortunate incidents in the childcare centres, that we then have evidence to support investigations and be able to give a comprehensive response to parents should they have concerns about their child's safety in preschools.

sections.label: Timing of earlier event
sections.summary: The speaker recalls that it was in June last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: To the best of my recollection, it was in June last year.

sections.label: No mandatory psychological screening
sections.summary: The speaker cautions against mandatory psychological screening, citing pre-employment checks and a self-declaration form requiring psychiatrist certification for declared mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: On the specific question of mandatory psychological screening, I would like to say that this is not done in other jurisdictions and this is not done for other professions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: While we fully appreciate the importance placed on child safety and we are taking a firm stance on child safety by having those pre-employment checks that I mentioned earlier for criminal antecedents, whether they have bad references and they must be certified fit and appropriate to work for the sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: But I would caution against mandatory psychological screening.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, I do not think that we should exclude these individuals who have mental health conditions if those mental health conditions are well managed from entering the preschool sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I would also like to share that currently there is a self-declaration form that potential educators have to fill up and this self-declaration form requires them to fill in whether or not they have mental health conditions and if they so declare that they have mental health conditions, then there will be need for a certification by a psychiatrist that they are able to work with young children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, I think that is the balance that we have to put in place to ensure child safety while ensuring that we do not stigmatise mental health conditions in our society.

sections.label: Parents' access to CCTV footage
sections.summary: ECDA said parents' access to CCTV footage is granted only to clarify feedback or assist investigation of serious incidents on reasonable grounds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: First and foremost, as shared in the media release by ECDA on the 31 August with regards to the mandatory installation of CCTV cameras, ECDA had shared that parents' access to CCTV footages will only be granted for the purposes of providing an objective reference point to clarify feedback or to assist the investigation of serious incidents within the preschool premises and the request has to be on reasonable grounds.

sections.label: Mandated CCTV installation by 1 July
sections.summary: The speaker says survey respondents should not give dishonest inputs and that CCTV installation was mandated by 1 July.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I am very sure the survey respondents know that they would have to provide the feedback to the best of their knowledge and that they really should not be providing dishonest inputs to an ECDA-conducted survey.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: But that said, I recognise the Member's concerns that even though some preschools may say that they have CCTVs but in actual fact, they may not and that is why we have mandated the CCTV installation by the 1 July.

sections.label: Mobile device policy and reporting
sections.summary: Operators' policies on personal mobile devices at work should not hinder staff from reporting wrongdoing in their centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: As I have said in my main response earlier, any operator's policy on the use of personal mobile devices at work should not hinder their staff from reporting from any wrongdoing in their centres.

sections.label: Reasonable policies and reporting channels
sections.summary: Operators' policies on personal mobile devices must be reasonable, and there are hotlines and email addresses for reporting wrongdoing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, while some operators have a policy on the use of personal mobile devices, it has to be a reasonable one.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I have also mentioned in my main reply that there are various channels for anyone to report wrongdoing – members of the public, educators – there are hotlines, email addresses in which any member of the public and educator can report wrongdoing.
